newsitem.title: GERMANY: Eurowings sees passengers up 10pct in first half.
newsitem.headline: Eurowings sees passengers up 10pct in first half.

text.p: German airline Eurowings Luftverkehrs AG said it increased passenger numbers 10 percent to 821,617 in the first half of 1996.
The seat load factor improved January-June by 1.3 percent to 56.4 percent, a company statement said.

Passenger numbers carried on scheduled services rose 15 percent to 795,502 but charter passenger levels declined 14 percent to 110,570, due to the loss of a contract with German airline Hapag-Lloyd, it added.

Eurowings marketing and finance director Ulrich Sigmann said in the statement: "This satisfying half-year result allows us to look forward to the second half with confidence and confirms our strategy of concentrating on European destinations."

Privately-owned Eurowings said it flies its own services to European destinations and also provides connecting services from Germany to Amsterdam for KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV and to Paris for Air France. - Air Cargo Newsroom tel:+44 171 542 7706 fax:+44 171 542 5017
